what_this_is: How far into this twin a given identity can reach. GitHub verifies identity and expresses access as repository permissions; the twin borrows both rather than inventing an auth system.

T0.name: GLOBAL
T0.gate: publish gate must pass; manual opt-in per stream

T1.name: AUTHENTICATED
T1.who: a named GitHub account with read access
T1.mechanism: private repo, counterparty added as a read collaborator
T1.gate: publish gate must pass; existence is hidden from everyone else (404)

T2.name: COLLABORATOR
T2.who: a named GitHub account with write access
T2.mechanism: private repo, counterparty added as a write collaborator
T2.gate: scoped by an explicit meeting grant; both sides can append

T3.name: PRIVATE
T3.mechanism: local only, no remote, excluded from every egg
T3.gate: never published at any tier; queryable only by the twin

rules: a stream's tier is declared, never inferred
promotion toward GLOBAL is manual and one-way — nothing becomes public by drift
the publish gate runs at every boundary regardless of intent
T3 is never published at any tier, for any counterparty, under any grant
to_request_access: Ask the business to add your GitHub account to the private DOGG as a read collaborator (T1) or a write collaborator (T2). There is nothing else to sign up for.
